# Stock from scraps

A freezer bag collects onion skins, carrot peelings, parsley stalks, mushroom trimmings and chicken carcasses through the week. Nothing that still has flavour goes in the bin. When the bag is full I tip it into the big pot, cover with cold water and simmer gently for two hours with a bay leaf and a few peppercorns.

The scraps would otherwise be waste, and the resulting stock beats anything from a carton. I strain it, cool it quickly and freeze it in jars of different sizes: small for sauces, large for soups. Avoid cabbage peelings and beetroot, which overpower everything.

Making stock this way turns leftovers into the base of next week's meals, and the habit costs nothing but a little freezer space.
